title: Reading together
hook: study groups, sutta circles, reading with a friend
tomorrow: one book fits in Mai's bag. who gets to choose it?

segments.voice: Yesterday was reading slowly: one line, then silence, the way Bahiya heard a few words alone in the street. Today the other half of reading: what happens when two people hold the same line?
screen: `ONE LINE, THEN SILENCE.` → `TWO PEOPLE, ONE LINE.`

segments.voice: Somebody in the group chat says let's start a book club, and then nobody reads the book. Ananda, the Buddha's attendant, had a better time with company. In the Samyutta Nikaya he comes to the Buddha with something warm to say: having good friends, good companions, is half of the holy life. A generous thing to say about friendship. And the Buddha's answer begins, strangely: don't say that, Ananda. Why would the teacher push back on praise for friends?
screen: `THE BOOK CLUB NOBODY READS FOR.` → `GOOD FRIENDS: HALF THE HOLY LIFE.` → `DON'T SAY THAT, ANANDA.`

segments.voice: Because Ananda undersold it. The Buddha goes on: it isn't half. Good friendship, kalyana-mittata, is the whole of the holy life. Someone with good friends can be expected to walk the whole path. Then he makes it personal: people caught in birth, aging and death are set free by having him as their good friend. That's the puzzle solved. He isn't correcting Ananda for loving friendship too much. Ananda didn't rate it high enough. And it's the teaching behind how Buddhists read. Tradition says the first teachings were kept by monks reciting them together, out loud, before anyone wrote them down. Now there are sutta circles in living rooms and on video calls: someone reads a passage aloud, the group sits in silence, then each person says what they heard. Notice what that adds to yesterday's single line. Nobody has to be the expert; the reading is the teacher, and the silence is shared. Alone, you hear what you're ready to hear. Together, someone hears what you missed, and you catch what they missed. In this sutta, a good friend on the path isn't a nice extra beside the practice. The friend is how the path gets walked.
screen: `NOT HALF: THE WHOLE.` · `KALYANA-MITTATA: ADMIRABLE FRIENDSHIP.` · `KEPT BY RECITING TOGETHER.` · `EACH HEARS WHAT THE OTHER MISSED.` · then, large: `TOGETHER.`

segments.voice: Choose one line you've read this year, from any text you love. Send it to one person you trust, just the line, nothing added. Then sit for two minutes with the same words, knowing someone else is holding them too.
Reading together: the same line held by two people, each hearing what the other missed.
Keep this one: together, because Ananda said half and the Buddha said the whole. Back tomorrow.

howItsDone: Buddhist study groups, sometimes called sutta circles or dharma study groups, meet in homes, temples and online: a passage is read aloud, the group sits in silence, and then each person shares what they heard.

fork.setup: your sutta circle reads a passage. one member jumps in to explain what it 'really means' before anyone else speaks. what fits today's teaching?
options: ask for a minute of silence, then let each person say what they heard
let the best-read person explain; that's what a good friend is for
skip the talking and just move on to the next passage
fork.reveal: reading together works because each person hears what the others missed. the friend matters as a fellow listener, not only as an explainer.

original.note: Pali: a good or admirable friend, one who walks the path with you. In this sutta the Buddha calls himself one.

trapdoor: what you thought: reading Buddhist texts is a private, solitary thing.
what it means: the Buddha told Ananda good friendship isn't half the holy life but the whole, so reading together is part of the path.
what a scholar hears: the Upaddha Sutta (SN 45.2), where kalyana-mittata is called the whole of the brahmacariya, the holy life.
guess: sharing a text aloud with others and hearing them
taking turns so the book gets finished sooner
quietly reading the same book in separate rooms

chat.says: Ava wants to read with me on video every sunday while i'm gone. she's not Buddhist. does that count?
options: it counts. a friend reading with you isn't half the path, the Buddha said. it's the whole.
only if Ava is Buddhist too. a sutta circle is just for people on one path.
not really. reading is a private practice; Bahiya was freed alone in the street.
chat.meaning: Ananda called good friendship half the holy life; the Buddha said it's the whole. A friend who reads with you is part of the path.

tie.story: Ananda praised good friends as half the holy life, and the Buddha said no: they're the whole of it.
tie.friend: Mai can say yes to Ava's Sunday calls; a friend holding the same line with her is the path, not a distraction.
tie.you: who would you like to read one line with?

Samyutta Nikaya.meaning: a collection of the Buddha's shorter teachings, grouped by topic

kalyana-mittata.meaning: Pali for admirable friendship on the path

sutta.meaning: a teaching of the Buddha; a discourse

sources.ref: Cullavagga XI (the first recitation of the teachings)

notes: SN 45.2 paraphrased: Ananda says admirable friendship is half the holy life; the Buddha: 'Not so, Ananda', it is the whole; beings subject to birth, aging and death are freed through him as their admirable friend. Confirm the paraphrase.
'Tradition says the first teachings were kept by monks reciting them together' refers to the account of the first council (Cullavagga XI); kept hedged as tradition. Confirm.
